what_its_for: Sodium oxybate is used to treat narcolepsy, a sleep disorder. It helps reduce sudden muscle weakness triggered by emotions (called cataplexy) and helps you stay awake during the day. It works while you sleep at night to improve the quality of your sleep.
how_to_take: Mix each dose with about 2 ounces (60 mL) of water in the child-resistant cups that come with your medication. Take your first dose right when you get into bed and plan to stay in bed for at least 8 hours. Set an alarm to take your second dose 2.5 to 4 hours later. Lie back down immediately after taking the second dose. Take this medicine on an empty stomach — do not eat for at least 2 hours before taking it. Never mix sodium oxybate with alcohol or sleep medicines.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks to find what works best for you. The usual starting dose is 4.5 grams per night, split into two equal doses. The dose may be increased up to 9 grams per night total, based on how well it works and how you tolerate it. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions — never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss your first dose of the night and you have already gone to bed, skip it and take only the second dose at the usual time. Never double up on doses. If you miss your second dose, just skip it — do not take it when you wake up in the morning. Talk to your doctor if you are regularly missing doses.
storage: Store sodium oxybate at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in the original bottle with the safety cap tightly closed. After you mix a dose with water, use it right away or within 24 hours if kept in the provided cup at room temperature. Keep this medicine locked up and out of reach of children and pets. Because of its potential for misuse, it must be kept in a secure location at all times.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink any alcohol while taking sodium oxybate — this combination can be life-threatening. Do not take sleep aids, anxiety medicines, opioid pain medicines, or other medicines that make you drowsy without first talking to your doctor. Do not drive, operate machinery, or do anything that requires full alertness for at least 6 hours after taking your last dose. Do not eat for at least 2 hours before your first nighttime dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: difficulty breathing or slow, shallow breathing while sleeping; confusion or unusual behavior after taking the medicine; sleepwalking or doing activities while not fully awake; signs of depression or thoughts of harming yourself; severe nausea or vomiting; bedwetting that is new or worsening; feeling extremely confused or disoriented in the morning. Also contact your doctor if the medication does not seem to be helping after a few weeks.
when_it_works: Most people begin to notice improvement in their symptoms within a few weeks, but it may take 8 to 12 weeks of gradual dose increases to feel the full benefit. Improvements in cataplexy and daytime sleepiness often happen together. Keep taking the medicine as prescribed even if you do not notice immediate results.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over) may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and confusion and should be monitored closely. This medicine is only approved for people age 7 and older for narcolepsy with cataplexy. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this medicine, as safety has not been fully established. People with breathing problems, sleep apnea, or liver disease should use this medicine with extra caution and under close medical supervision. Sodium oxybate is a controlled substance and is only available through a special restricted pharmacy program called a REMS program — your doctor must enroll you in this program before you can receive the medication.
